title: Sum of Both Diagonals
statement:
You get a square grid grid of size n × n. Add up every cell on the main diagonal (top-left to bottom-right) and every cell on the other diagonal (top-right to bottom-left).

When n is odd the two diagonals cross in the centre cell. Count that cell only once. Return the total.

examples.why: Main diagonal 2 + 3 + 5, other diagonal 1 + 4, plus the shared centre 3 only once: 15.
With even n the diagonals do not share a cell, so all four cells count.
The single cell is on both diagonals but counts once.

gen: (r, big) => { const n = big ? 100 : r.int(1, 6); return [r.matrix(n, n, 1, 100)]; }
hints: Which cells are on the main diagonal? Which are on the other one? Write the condition on row i and column j.
Main diagonal: j = i. Other diagonal: j = n − 1 − i. You only need one loop over i.
The two coincide only when i = n − 1 − i, which happens for exactly one row when n is odd. Subtract that cell once.

explain.intuition:
Each row holds exactly one cell of each diagonal: column i for the main one and column n − 1 − i for the other. So one pass over the rows picks up both, with no need to visit the other cells.

The only trap is the centre. When n is odd, the middle row's two columns are the same cell, and adding both would count it twice.
steps: For each row i, add grid[i][i] and grid[i][n − 1 − i].
If n is odd, subtract the centre grid[mid][mid] once.
pitfalls: Counting the centre cell twice for odd n.
Subtracting a centre for even n, where the diagonals never meet.

solutions.title: Check every cell
solutions.idea: Visit every cell and add it if it lies on either diagonal. The "or" counts the centre once by itself.

solutions.title: One pass over the rows
solutions.idea: Take both diagonal cells from each row, then remove the centre once when n is odd.

followups: Return the sums of every diagonal running top-left to bottom-right, one per diagonal. How do you index them?
The grid is m × n, not square. What does "the other diagonal" mean now, and what changes?
